correctness.rationale: For all 495 possible four-row sets, 21 complete affine orbits are enumerated. The 495 columns for each orbit representative are fully checked, with identical results from exact Z[zeta_12] 24-term determinant reduction and F61 Gaussian eliminations at all four primitive twelfth roots. The four-root test is logically exact because reduced polynomial degree <=3 and all coefficient absolute values <=24 <61. All orbit counts and incidence totals, the 20-level distribution and the equal-occupancy counterexample are algebraically verified. No unproved infinite extrapolation or tolerance-based decision.

value.rationale: The exact defect count is a motivated quantitative invariant: how many four-sample patterns fail for a given Fourier row selection, not merely whether at least one fails. The small mixed-primary nonsquarefree order 12 has twenty distinct counts among 21 affine row types; the existing Boolean full-spark classification cannot recover this distribution. The exact 15-versus-27 pair with identical divisor-occupancy data is a substantive structural boundary for using residue statistics to predict quantitative Fourier sampling failure. The full census is natural, complete, and verifiable, with future use for erasure failure profiles; it is not an arbitrary slice or routine size increment.
